process_area.title: Human Rights Policy, Salient-Risk Identification & Due Diligence Framework

value_stream.name: Human Rights, Modern Slavery & Responsible Supply Chain Due Diligence

fields.Participants: Sustainability (links to VS-25), Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34/VS-122), Legal (links to VS-100), HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), Compliance (links to VS-119), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Board (links to VS-36), Global Sourcing (links to VS-122)
fields.Trigger: Program stand-up; annual review; regulatory change

workflows.name: Human Rights & Responsible Sourcing Policy, Commitments & Governance

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "establish governance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-capture of "CEO/Board ratify the policy, approve the budget/resources, and cascade" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: dedicated program; operational: HRDD framework (W4003)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-owner risk**: Human rights unowned beyond ESG-reporting mention; mitigated by dedicated program
- **Policy-without-execution risk**: Commitments not operationalized; mitigated by HRDD framework (W4003)
System Touchpoints: - ESG (links to VS-25); procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-34); legal (links to VS-100); HR (links to VS-19/VS-103); governance (links to VS-36); global sourcing (links to VS-122)

steps.activity: Sustainability/ESG Manager/VP Legal & Compliance define the human-rights & responsible-sourcing policy aligned to the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs), ILO core conventions, the UN Global Compact, and Philippine labor law (links to VS-84/VS-19); cover own operations and the full supply chain; set commitments (zero forced/child labor, living-wage direction, freedom of association, responsible recruitment, no land-rights harm)
steps.r: Sustainability/ESG Manager / VP Legal & Compliance / Sustainability

steps.activity: Sustainability/ESG Manager establish governance: a cross-functional responsible-sourcing steering (Procurement, Merchandising, Legal, HR, Compliance, Global Sourcing), decision rights, the integration with vendor management (VS-03), ESG (VS-25), ethics/speak-up (VS-119), and audit (VS-21), and KPIs
CEO/Board ratify the policy, approve the budget/resources, and cascade as a board-level enterprise risk (links to VS-21.2 ERM and VS-36 governance); publish externally and to suppliers

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement/Global Sourcing (links to VS-122/VS-03), Insights (links to VS-44), Legal, HR, external human-rights advisors, stakeholders

workflows.name: Salient Human Rights Risk Identification & Materiality Assessment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-identify of "identify salient human-rights risks across BuildRight's operations and supply…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-register of "Sustainability prioritize salient risks and the supply-chain tiers/geographies/categories where" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document the saliency assessment, retain evidence, and feed it into the HRDD…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: UNGP lens and geography/category mapping; operational: annual cycle and event triggers
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-scoping risk**: Saliency missing key risks (e.g., deeper-tier minerals); mitigated by UNGP lens and geography/category mapping
- **Static-assessment risk**: Saliency not refreshed; mitigated by annual cycle and event triggers
System Touchpoints: - ESG (links to VS-25.2); procurement/global sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122); insights (links to VS-44); ERM (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Procurement identify salient human-rights risks across BuildRight's operations and supply chain using the UNGP saliency lens (scale, scope, irremediability): forced/modern-slavery labor, child labor, unsafe conditions, wage/hour violations, discrimination, freedom-of-association limits, migrant-labor abuse, and community/land-rights impacts — mapped by category (tools/electronics, paint/chemicals, lumber, tiles, PPE, garden/agro) and sourcing geography

Sustainability prioritize salient risks and the supply-chain tiers/geographies/categories where they concentrate (tier-1 vendors, tier-2 component/material suppliers, raw-material origin), and integrate findings into ESG materiality (links to VS-25.2) and the ERM risk register (links to VS-21.2)
Sustainability document the saliency assessment, retain evidence, and feed it into the HRDD framework (W4003), risk modeling (W4006), and reporting (links to PA-131.3)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34/VS-122), Legal, Compliance (links to VS-119), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), HR, affected business units

workflows.name: Human Rights Due Diligence (HRDD) Framework & Operating Model

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "Sustainability/ESG Manager/Procurement establish the HRDD framework per UNGP" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor risk intelligence, refresh saliency" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-623 (ensure controlled execution — Human Rights Policy, Salient-Risk Identification & Due Diligence Framework (PA-131.1).)
- operational: gates and contract safeguards; operational: risk-based tiering
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bolt-on risk**: HRDD not embedded in procurement decisions; mitigated by gates and contract safeguards
- **Inconsistent-intensity risk**: Same DD for low- and high-risk suppliers; mitigated by risk-based tiering
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-34/VS-122); vendor mgmt (links to VS-67); audit (links to VS-21); ESG (links to VS-25); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/ESG Manager/Procurement establish the HRDD framework per UNGP: identify and assess (W4009), act on impacts (prevent/mitigate/remediate — W4010–W4014), track effectiveness (W4019), and communicate (W4020/W4021); define risk-based intensity (enhanced DD for high-risk categories/geographies)

Sustainability/ESG Manager/Procurement embed HRDD into the procurement lifecycle: sourcing/onboarding gates (links to VS-03.1/VS-122.2), contract safeguards (W4005), PO and order allocation (links to VS-03.2), and supplier management (links to VS-67) — making human-rights DD a prerequisite to doing business

Sustainability/ESG Manager/Sustainability operate continuous HRDD: monitor risk intelligence, refresh saliency (W4002), and coordinate remediation/grievance (W4012/W4013) and responsible disengagement (W4014)

fields.Participants: Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Global Sourcing (links to VS-122), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Master Data (links to VS-29), Sustainability, IT (links to VS-27/VS-113)
fields.Trigger: HRDD framework; traceability need; B2B customer/regulatory requirement

workflows.name: Supply Chain Mapping, Transparency & Traceability Program

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "technology — distinct from anti-counterfeit serialization" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "Procurement/Sustainability maintain the map, refresh on sourcing change, identify" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-623 (ensure controlled execution — Human Rights Policy, Salient-Risk Identification & Due Diligence Framework (PA-131.1).)
- operational: tier-2 mapping for salient categories; operational: refresh on change and disclosure in contracts
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tier-2-blindness risk**: Unknown sub-tier suppliers hide risks; mitigated by tier-2 mapping for salient categories
- **Data-staleness risk**: Map out of date; mitigated by refresh on change and disclosure in contracts
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-122); MDM (links to VS-29); IT (links to VS-27/VS-113); anti-counterfeit (links to VS-71); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Procurement/Global-Sourcing map the supply chain: tier-1 vendors, key tier-2 (component/material) suppliers, and raw-material origins (minerals, timber, latex, cotton, palm) for salient categories — capturing geography, factory/site, and certifications

Procurement/IT build transparency/traceability: supplier disclosure (factories, subcontracting), tier-2 mapping for high-risk categories, product-origin/attributes in the item master (links to VS-29), and (where warranted) traceability technology — distinct from anti-counterfeit serialization (VS-71)
Procurement/Sustainability maintain the map, refresh on sourcing change, identify transparency gaps and blind spots, and feed risk modeling (W4006) and reporting (W4020)

fields.Participants: Procurement (links to VS-03), Legal (links to VS-100), Compliance (links to VS-119), Sustainability, Global Sourcing (links to VS-122)
fields.Trigger: Vendor onboarding (links to VS-03.1); contract renewal

workflows.name: Supplier Code of Conduct, Onboarding & Contractual Safeguards

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "Sustainability/ESG Manager/Legal maintain the Supplier Code of Conduct" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-inspect of "inspection rights, remediation obligations, termination for breach, and…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track acknowledgment/adherence, integrate with vendor scorecard" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-623 (ensure controlled execution — Human Rights Policy, Salient-Risk Identification & Due Diligence Framework (PA-131.1).)
- operational: audit rights and consequences; operational: contractual flow-down
Pain Points / Risks: - **Paper-code risk**: Code signed without enforcement; mitigated by audit rights and consequences
- **Flow-down-gap risk**: Obligations not reaching sub-tiers; mitigated by contractual flow-down
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-67/VS-122); legal/contracts (links to VS-100); ABC (links to VS-86); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/ESG Manager/Legal maintain the Supplier Code of Conduct (labor standards, no forced/child labor, wage/hour, health & safety, freedom of association, non-discrimination, responsible recruitment, environmental, anti-bribery links to VS-86, sub-tier disclosure, and the right to audit) aligned to BuildRight's own commitments (W4001)

Procurement/Legal require code acknowledgment and contractual safeguards on onboarding (links to VS-03.1/VS-122.2) and renewal: flow-down to sub-tiers, audit/inspection rights, remediation obligations, termination for breach, and data/transparency obligations
Procurement track acknowledgment/adherence, integrate with vendor scorecard (links to VS-67), and enforce consequences for non-compliance (links to W4014)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement/Global Sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122), Insights (links to VS-44), external risk-intelligence/data providers, Legal
fields.Trigger: HRDD framework; supply-chain mapping (W4004); new category/geography

workflows.name: Modern Slavery, Forced Labor & Child Labor Risk Modeling

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "Sustainability/Procurement model modern-slavery/forced-labor/child-labor risk per vendor, category, and geography" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-flag of "flag high-risk vendors/categories/geographies for enhanced DD" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor for emerging risks" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: multi-source indices and intelligence; operational: annual cycle and event triggers
Pain Points / Risks: - **False-negative risk**: Model missing high-risk vendors; mitigated by multi-source indices and intelligence
- **Stale-model risk**: Risk not refreshed; mitigated by annual cycle and event triggers
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/global sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122); insights (links to VS-44); ABC/sanctions (links to VS-86); records (links to VS-88); ESG (links to VS-25)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Procurement model modern-slavery/forced-labor/child-labor risk per vendor, category, and geography using indices (e.g., Global Slavery Index), sector risk (tools/electronics, PPE/apparel, lumber, garden/agro, minerals), and intelligence (media, NGO, sanctions links to VS-86, import-detention data)

Sustainability/Procurement tier vendors into risk bands (low/enhanced/high), flag high-risk vendors/categories/geographies for enhanced DD (links to W4009), and prioritize audits (W4010) and traceability (W4004)
Sustainability refresh the model on change, monitor for emerging risks (new evidence, regulatory watchlists), and feed findings into sourcing decisions (links to W4014/W4009) and reporting (W4020)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Legal, HR (links to VS-19), Compliance (links to VS-119), external auditors

workflows.name: Responsible Recruitment, Migrant Labor & Recruitment-Fee Controls

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document-retention and movement-restriction indicators" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with BuildRight's own contingent-workforce practices" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-validate of "verify via audit" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: audit and worker voice; operational: remediation tracking (W4012)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hidden-debt-bondage risk**: Recruitment-fee abuse undetected; mitigated by audit and worker voice
- **Remediation-failure risk**: Fees not reimbursed; mitigated by remediation tracking (W4012)
System Touchpoints: - Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122); legal/contracts (links to VS-100); contingent workforce (links to VS-98); audit (links to VS-21); ESG (links to VS-25)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Procurement assess responsible-recruitment risk: migrant-labor prevalence in sourcing geographies (factory/field), recruitment-fee/debt-bondage exposure, document-retention and movement-restriction indicators, and the "Employer Pays" principle (no worker fees for employment)

Procurement/Legal embed responsible-recruitment contractual safeguards (no worker-paid recruitment fees, document retention by worker, no movement restriction) and require evidence from high-risk vendors; coordinate with BuildRight's own contingent-workforce practices (links to VS-98)
Sustainability verify via audit (links to W4010/W4011), remediate where fees paid (reimbursement), and report (W4020); engage stakeholders (W4021)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement/Global Sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122), Legal, Insights (links to VS-44), external advisors, stakeholders

workflows.name: Conflict-Affected, Indigenous Peoples & Land-Rights Risk Assessment

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Sustainability/Procurement require evidence" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-document of "document findings, engage stakeholders" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: certification and legality evidence; operational: FPIC and restrictions
Pain Points / Risks: - **Deforestation/illegal-timber risk**: Lumber from illegal/contested sources; mitigated by certification and legality evidence
- **Community-harm risk**: Sourcing causing indigenous/land-rights harm; mitigated by FPIC and restrictions
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/global sourcing (links to VS-03/VS-122); insights (links to VS-44); ABC/sanctions (links to VS-86); anti-counterfeit (links to VS-71); ESG (links to VS-25); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Procurement assess land-rights, indigenous-peoples, and conflict-affected-area risk for raw-material sourcing (timber/lumber legality and deforestation links to VS-25.2, minerals from conflict-affected areas, palm/latex, quarrying for tiles/cement), using source intelligence and certification (FSC, PEFC for timber)

Sustainability/Procurement require evidence (legality, certification, free-prior-informed-consent where relevant) and embed sourcing restrictions for high-risk origins; coordinate with anti-counterfeit/anti-illegal-logging concerns (links to VS-71) and sanctions (links to VS-86)
Sustainability document findings, engage stakeholders (W4021), and report (W4020); refresh on change
